modules.title: What is AI?
modules.blurb: A working mental model: what an LLM actually does, the vocabulary, why data decides everything, and a delegation heuristic you can carry under pressure.

modules.title: Choosing the tool for the task
modules.blurb: Chat assistants, copilots, and the AI already embedded in your HR stack — what each is actually for, and how to tell a language model from a scoring engine before you rely on either.

modules.title: What it costs and how it scales
modules.blurb: Tokens, context windows, and pricing — enough of the economics to size a use case, read a vendor quote, and know when a bigger model is worth it.

modules.title: Working with your documents and data
modules.blurb: Attachments, long documents, and sensitive material: getting your world into the model's view without crowding out the question — or crossing a line your legal team hasn't cleared.

modules.title: Prompting as briefing
modules.blurb: Role, task, context, format. Prompting as briefing a capable stranger — and iteration as the keystone behavior that separates fluent users from frustrated ones.

modules.title: When it's confidently wrong
modules.blurb: Hallucination in depth: why fluent output deserves more scrutiny, not less, and the verification habits that keep a fabricated citation out of a document with someone's name on it.

modules.title: The lines that don't move
modules.blurb: Bias, adverse impact, and decisions about people. Where AI assists, where it must stop, and how to say so in a way your organization will actually follow.

modules.title: What you own
modules.blurb: Data agreements, disclosure, and accountability. What you're responsible for when AI touched the work — and the policy questions to settle before someone asks.

modules.title: From one-offs to workflows
modules.blurb: The workflow lens: five parts every repeatable workflow has, the audit that finds your candidates, the selection rules — and the capstone's first stage: pick your build and spec it.

modules.title: Context that keeps
modules.blurb: The artisan tax and its refund: context packs — what's durable, what arrives fresh, what never becomes infrastructure — built hands-on in your organization's tools.

modules.title: Document pipelines
modules.blurb: Chains with checkpoints: structure forward, prose last, and the lossy middle where detail dies. Your workflow becomes a pipeline and runs on real material.

modules.title: Verification by design
modules.blurb: The verification budget: sized to stakes, matched to failure mode, cheap enough to survive week six — plus the sign-off that means something and the path for when something ships wrong anyway.

modules.title: Handing it to an agent
modules.blurb: The autonomy ladder, priced in evidence: draft-only, propose-then-approve, act-with-audit-trail. Guardrails as permissions, the decision-laundering test, and the refusal as a senior artifact.

modules.title: People data in production
modules.blurb: Four tiers, the person-test, redaction as a pipeline step, the agreement layer, and a blame-safe escalation path. The boundary sheet that makes your workflow deployable.

modules.title: The operating rhythm
modules.blurb: Seconds per run, ten a week, twenty a month. Four honest numbers with a baseline, retirement criteria written in advance — and the reckoning against your Module 1 prediction.

modules.title: Ship it and prove it
modules.blurb: The capstone lands: the consistency pass, the handoff test with a cold reader, and the executive sentence with receipts. Completes the jump to Practitioner.

courses.title: AI 101 · Foundations
courses.blurb: From The Risk to The Novice: a working mental model, honest calibration, and the judgment to know what to hand over.

courses.title: AI 201 · The Practitioner
courses.blurb: Workflows that stick: one real build advanced across eight modules. Module 1 is open — designed to follow AI 101, and open to the adventurous either way.

courses.title: AI 301 · The Translator
courses.blurb: Leading adoption beyond your own desk: coaching other functions, evaluating vendors, and running pilots that produce evidence instead of anecdotes.

courses.title: AI 401 · The Steward
courses.blurb: Policy, risk, and governance: owning the organizational answer to what AI may touch, who verifies it, and how you'll know when it goes wrong.
